open_points.subject: contract_only eligibility
open_points.text: when each of its fields names a fact a model here already lists and the row itself has no product meaning of its own
open_points.question: What objective rule determines whether the relationship represented by a table row has no product meaning and therefore may lack a State 1 model record?
options: A row is contract_only whenever all individual fields already occur in recorded models
A row is contract_only only when both its fields and every relationship among them are mechanically derived from an already-decided rule
The owner decides contract_only status separately for every row model
open_points.default_guess: Require the fields and their relationship to be mechanically derivable from an already-decided rule.

open_points.subject: ConfirmedOwnerAction
open_points.text: `ConfirmedOwnerAction`, the row of the data provider's `CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS`, is one
open_points.question: What model kind and identity does ConfirmedOwnerAction have, and who creates its runtime instances from what source?
options: It is an ordinary runtime value model instantiated by the data provider from a ConfirmedAction and an owner action
It is read-only specification data with kind `mapping` or `catalog` and never becomes a runtime DTO
It is not a model; the contracts merely repeat its two fields wherever needed
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an ordinary value model instantiated by the data provider from the two declared vocabulary members.

witness.initial: The release contains `CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS` and code needs one of its rows.
events: The data provider assembles its release constants.
outcomes: The provider constructs a typed ConfirmedOwnerAction value with value identity.
No ConfirmedOwnerAction value exists; consumers receive an unmodelled contract shape or two separate values.
witness.observer: The data provider, generated code, and model-closure checker

open_points.subject: CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS correspondence
open_points.text: Such a row adds no fact, so State 6 still adds no fact a model does not list here.
open_points.question: Does the pairing of a confirmed action with an owner action constitute a model fact, even though each member is already a fact of another model?
options: Yes; each allowed pairing is a correspondence fact that must be listed by a State 1 model
No; the pairing is wholly derived from State 2 A13 rule 6 and the ConfirmedAction vocabulary
Only the existence of the table is a fact; its individual pairings are not
open_points.default_guess: Treat each pairing as derived only if the cited rule and vocabulary uniquely determine it; otherwise record the correspondence as a model fact.

witness.initial: Two confirmed actions and two owner actions exist.
events: The data provider chooses which confirmed action is paired with which owner action.
The owner submits one action with a confirmation value.
outcomes: The chosen pairing is a normative fact carried by the table row.
The pairing is not a fact of the row and must be derived independently from the cited rule and vocabulary.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees whether the submitted action is accepted

open_points.subject: CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS source of truth
open_points.text: the rule the table serves — an action that asks for confirmation is submitted with the confirmation value the step showed — is fixed by State 2 A13 rule 6 and the `ConfirmedAction` vocabulary, the closed list of the actions that ask for confirmation ("Identity formats").
open_points.question: Which source uniquely determines the table's rows, and which source prevails if A13 rule 6, the ConfirmedAction vocabulary, and CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS do not imply the same action-to-confirmation correspondence?
options: A13 rule 6 and the vocabulary are authoritative and the table is derived from them
The contract declaration is authoritative and the other texts only explain it
open_points.default_guess: Make A13 rule 6 plus the vocabulary authoritative and require the table to be an exact derived projection.

witness.initial: A confirmed action is present in the vocabulary, but its table row names a different owner action from the one inferred from A13.
events: The owner starts the action and receives a confirmation value.
The owner submits the displayed value with that action.
outcomes: Registry follows A13 and the vocabulary and accepts the submission.
Registry follows CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS and refuses it or executes the differently paired action.

open_points.subject: CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS consumption
open_points.text: the rule the table serves — an action that asks for confirmation is submitted with the confirmation value the step showed
open_points.question: Which product action reads CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS, if any: showing the confirmation step, submitting the confirmed owner action, both, or neither?
options: No product action reads it; generated code derives the same rule elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Use it in both the step that issues the confirmation and the submission that validates it.

witness.initial: An owner action requires confirmation and its row is present in CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS.
events: The owner opens the confirmation step.
The owner submits the action with the value shown.
outcomes: Both actions use the table and agree on the pairing.
Neither action is required to read the table and one derives a different pairing from the prose rule.

open_points.subject: ConfirmedOwnerAction
open_points.text: A row of a constant table may be declared by the contracts alone (`contract_only`), with no record of its own here, when each of its fields names a fact a model here already lists and the row itself has no product meaning of its own; its declaration names where the product rule the table serves is fixed.
open_points.rule:
Каждая runtime-модель без `kind` обязана объявлять
  `identity: "value"|"entity"`; модели с `kind` поле `identity` не содержат.
open_points.question: The passage must require every contract-only table-row runtime model either to declare `identity: "value"|"entity"` or to declare one of the registered non-runtime `kind` values; it cannot leave the row only in contracts without either classification.
